children: OTTAWA--Any trade pact Canada strikes with the U.S. must ensure that agreed-upon tariff levels on certain goods would not be subject to change, Prime Minister Mark Carneys said.

Those assurances were not provided in talks last month, Carney said, which then collapsed and triggered new U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, and proposed retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa set to take effect on Tuesday.

"There needs to be some stability and credibility" in any future trade pact, Carney told reporters at a press event in Thunder Bay, Ontario. He said Canada sought assurances that agreed-upon tariffs on steel, aluminum and automobiles would not be subject to change. The U.S. and Canada had tentatively agreed upon sharp reductions on existing tariffs covering specific sectors, The Wall Street Journal reported.

"There were a few instances in the negotiations where those protections were not going to be given, and in fact, the opposite was going to be inserted, which is unacceptable," Carney said. This marks a further elaboration from the Canadian leader on why negotiations suddenly broke down after officials just days earlier were optimistic that a deal was imminent.

The White House said this week that Canada was offered the most generous trade deal among America's trading partners. Instead, Canada rejected the proposal, and made further demands and offered little in return, the White House said.

Earlier in the week, Carney criticized taunting of Canada by U.S. officials, and said it was not constructive toward resolving outstanding trade issues. President Trump has threatened to impose a potentially-crippling 50% tariff on Canadian-made motor vehicles and auto parts starting Jan. 1. In the Oval Office on Wednesday, Trump reiterated that the U.S. doesn't need Canadian goods, citing energy and forest products.

title: U.S. Failed to Give Assurances on Tariff Levels, Canada's Carney Says
